products.title: Slippery Willie's Stupid, Ugly Shoes
products.description: Review "Slippery Willie's Stupid, Ugly Shoes", by L. T. Peters---This adorable work is the first published children's book by Pinellas Park's L. T. Peters. I't's the story of Willie, a boy who doesn't walk. He slips. But then he gets some special--crazy looking--shoes. He's afraid kids at school will laugh at him for wearing the huge, red, yellow, and blue clodhoppers. And they do. And so do teachers, truck drivers, cats, dogs, birds, people in planes. Then he discovers it was all a dream. Later, when he really wears his shoes to school, no one laughs. In fact,the kids want shoes just like his." -- Book Review---Tampa Tribune, Sunday, March 9, 2008 by Karen Haymon Long, Tribune Book Editor "So many of our kids here at Gilda's Club can identify with feeling different in school and your book touched on that sensitive issue with an appropriate sense of humor---the kids LOVED it. Thank you so much." -- Amy Plain, E.C.E, B.A.A., C.L.S Noogieland Program Coordinator, Gilda's Club, Greater Toronto "What a delightful story. Best wishes." -- Gilda's Club, Delaware Valley (Warminster, PA) Cathy Kalinowski, MSS, LSW Noogieland Mgr 1)I liked it. It was funny and sweet. Love, Catie 2)I love it but write one on clothes. love, Isabella 3)I liked how he slid all over and everyone laughed at his stupid shoes. from Joshua G. 4)Honestly, I really didn't like it. It is my honest opinion. I don't like comedy. Sincerely, Heaven 5)Did you write the story because you have slippery feet and stupid ugly shoes? from Brandon -- Mrs. Gaskill's 4th Grade Class,Pasadena Fundamental School, St. Petersburg, FL 1)Yes, I loved you story. It was hilarious. Why did you write it? your friend, Daniel 2)I thought this book was great and I loved it and the big shoes was hilarious. Sincerely, Star 3)I loved your book can I have some for my friends. It made me and them laugh. Love, Selena 4)Thank you very much. we all enjoyed it. Mrs. Ritchie -- Bardmoor Elementary School, Seminole, FL Mrs. Ritchie's 3rd Grade Class From the Author This is dedicated to all kids who think they are "different". It does not matter how tall or short you are, how big your nose is,how fast you can run, how high you can jump,if you can see or not, hear or not, or even be wheelchair bound, you are all God's special individual creations because God "don't make no junk". About the Author L.T. Peters was born and raised in the Bronx in New York City. He has done free-lance work over the years writing many newspaper columns for local publications. This is his first published children's book. Peters has lived in Pinellas Park, Fl for the past 28 years. Excerpt. © Reprinted by permission. All rights reserved. -----"Willie could not ride a bike because his feet would slip off the pedals. He could not climb a tree because his feet slipped off the branches. -----why sometimes his shoes and socks would slide right off his feet even when he was just sitting at his desk in school. Poor Willie,he just slipped, slid, snd spun up, down, over, across, forwards, backwards, and sideways too. Read more

dialogue.user: I'm interested in **Call of the Canyon** and **The Spanish Game**. Could you tell me more about these two books?
dialogue.agent:
Here are the details for the books you're interested in:

**Call of the Canyon**
- Price: $15.76
- Average Rating: 5.0
- Number of Reviews: 1
- Rating Number: 8
- Features: Two Lives... Two Worlds... Heartbreak awaits. Call of the Canyon, second of the Waiting for Dusk series, continues the dramatic story of Kate Roberts and Drew Kelly. New challenges face the couple when Drew joins Kate in the present. Nothing is easy. Tyson’s still their nemesis, causing trouble whenever he can. Carl, Kate’s friend and neighbor, moves back home to Ohio and creates unexpected problems at the canyon. A wedding, a tragic accident, and a family broken by scandal affect both the past and present. And in the end, Kate may pay the ultimate price.

**The Spanish Game**
- Price: $17.95
- Average Rating: 5.0
- Number of Reviews: 1
- Rating Number: 3
- Features: Jennifer Ellis thought she had left behind the memories of the international incident where a chartered Iberian Air 727 was hijacked with she and other American high school students, including her brother. But eight years later, while working at the West Wing Gallery of the National Gallery of Art, Jennifer Ellis sees a figure involved with the incident. What was he doing in Washington, D.C.? Was he simply on vacation? If so, why did he run when he realized she'd seen him? Bent on revenge for the slaying of his family, and financed by a wealthy patron in Barcelona, Spain with his own grudge to bear, Ernesto de Rivera uses a unique and deadly high tech method of assassination. When de Rivera discovers that Henry Ellis was the one responsible for unleashing the terrorist who massacred his family he turns his attention to the Ellis family. Once again, the Ellis family is in danger. However, this time, the tables are turned. Instead of Henry Ellis trying to protect and save the lives of his children, it is his daughter, Jennifer Ellis, along with a female F.B.I. agent and a woman detective from Barcelona. Together they confront not only Ernesto de Rivera, but other heretofore unknown threats against their lives.

Would you like to know more about any specific book or proceed with a purchase?
